description: Fix drag-and-drop section reordering for Modern CV template — persist order to Supabase and propagate to Live Preview, Aperçu, PDF, and DOCX exports.

userStories.title: Explore current drag-and-drop and section ordering data model
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to understand how the editor drag-and-drop currently works, what state it updates, and how sections are rendered in the Modern template, so I can plan the fix.
acceptanceCriteria: Identify the editor components handling drag-and-drop for sidebar and main content sections
Identify what state or data structure is updated when a section is dragged and dropped
Identify whether the ordering is persisted to Supabase or only held in local React state
Identify the section keys used for sidebar and main content in the Modern template (e.g., 'skills', 'experience')
Identify how the Modern template renderer reads and orders sections in resume-preview.tsx
Document findings in progress.txt
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add section order fields to resume data model and persist on drop
userStories.description: As a user editing a Modern CV, I want my sidebar and main content section reordering to be saved to the database immediately when I drop a section, so my changes are not lost.
acceptanceCriteria: Resume JSONB content field supports sidebarSectionOrder (string[]) and mainSectionOrder (string[]) — or equivalent fields identified in US-001
When a user drags and drops a sidebar section, the new order is saved to Supabase immediately
When a user drags and drops a main content section, the new order is saved to Supabase immediately
Order persists across page refreshes
If no custom order is stored (existing resumes), the default section order is used as fallback
No changes to other templates' data or behavior
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Modern template Live Preview and Aperçu consume persisted section order
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Live Preview and Aperçu to immediately reflect the section order I configured via drag-and-drop, so I get instant visual feedback.
acceptanceCriteria: Modern template renderer in resume-preview.tsx reads sidebarSectionOrder and mainSectionOrder from resume data
Sidebar sections render in the persisted order
Main content sections render in the persisted order
After dropping a section, Live Preview updates in the same render cycle (no refresh needed)
Aperçu shows the same persisted order when opened
Fallback to default order when no custom order is stored
Only the Modern template rendering is affected — other templates unchanged
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: PDF export reflects persisted section order for Modern template
userStories.description: As a user, I want my PDF export to reflect the section order I configured via drag-and-drop, so the exported document matches my intent.
acceptanceCriteria: PDF export of a Modern CV renders sidebar sections in the persisted order
PDF export of a Modern CV renders main content sections in the persisted order
No changes to PDF export for other templates
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: DOCX export reflects persisted section order for Modern template
userStories.description: As a user, I want my DOCX export to reflect the section order I configured via drag-and-drop, so the exported Word document matches my intent.
acceptanceCriteria: docx-modern.ts reads sidebarSectionOrder and mainSectionOrder from resume data
DOCX export renders sidebar sections in the persisted order
DOCX export renders main content sections in the persisted order
Fallback to default order when no custom order is stored
No changes to DOCX export for other templates
Typecheck passes
